subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli live-session cleanup remain unconditional at turn end, or should OpenClaw add bounded drain and telemetry for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren?
rationale: The source confirms the reported cleanup behavior, but changing it affects orphan prevention, process-tree cleanup safety, model-visible terminal state, and likely config/default surfaces.

options.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
options.body: Add a narrow owner-approved contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing any forced cleanup to the parent/session.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep unconditional cleanup for now, but snapshot, log, or surface killed grandchildren so the silent failure class becomes observable before changing lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Keep cleanup as the contract
options.body: Document that Claude CLI Workflow/Bash grandchildren are not supported across OpenClaw turn boundaries and route long-running work to exec/process, ACP, or durable task surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Add a narrow owner-approved contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing any forced cleanup to the parent/session.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest recent Claude live-session history and owns the adjacent run-lifecycle reliability direction.
